def transform(grid):
    # Each framed panel's nested color sequence is reversed between input and output;
    # preserve zero background and map successive nonzero layers inward-to-outward.
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v)
    # Colors form nested layers; reverse their order by frequency (outermost layers have more cells).
    order=[c for c,n in cnt.most_common()]
    # stable frequency sort descending => layers outer to inner; reverse color mapping.
    mp={c:order[-1-i] for i,c in enumerate(order)}
    return [[0 if v==0 else mp[v] for v in row] for row in grid]
PY

cat > /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687872/attempts/0874d736f6374307823ec7507ddf4822/system/state/workspace/programs/task-56991e75.py <<'PY'
def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0]); out=[r[:] for r in grid]
    seen=set()
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]==0 or (r,c) in seen: continue
        stack=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
        while stack:
          y,x=stack.pop(); cells.append((y,x))
          for yy,xx in ((y-1,x),(y+1,x),(y,x-1),(y,x+1)):
            if 0<=yy<h and 0<=xx<w and grid[yy][xx]!=0 and (yy,xx) not in seen:
              seen.add((yy,xx)); stack.append((yy,xx))
        from collections import Counter
        counts=Counter(grid[y][x] for y,x in cells)
        layers=[v for v,n in counts.most_common()]
        # Rectangle layers have monotonically decreasing area from outside inward.
        mapping={layers[i]:layers[-1-i] for i in range(len(layers))}
        for y,x in cells: out[y][x]=mapping[grid[y][x]]
    return out
PY
